title: About MATKP
bodyHtml:
What is MATKP?

Adipose tissue regulates diverse metabolic processes and plays a role in the pathophysiology of diverse phenotypes. However, its development, subpopulations, and molecular pathways remain poorly understood. To address this challenge, we created the Mammalian Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal (MATKP), an open community portal for multi-species mammalian adipose biology. The MATKP aggregates data for adipose tissues and cell types, the genes active within them, and their relationship to human phenotypes. MATKP plans to offer reproducible analysis pipelines, wet lab and computational protocols, datasets, analyses, and visualizations for epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and imaging data.

If you use MATKP, please see our Policies for citation information.

 

What does MATKP offer currently?

MATKP integrates expert-curated datasets, with an initial focus on transcriptomics from human and mouse adipose tissues. Cell types, tissue depots, and metadata fields are harmonized across datasets using standard ontologies to enable cross-dataset standardization. From each dataset, users can obtain analyzed results and interactive visualizations through the Single Cell Browser, which enables interactive cell type clustering, marker gene identification, and more. The Differential Gene Expression Browser enables analysis of differential gene expression in various conditions using bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data and pseudobulk analysis of single cell RNA-seq data. Additionally, users can explore adipose-relevant phenotypes or gene information.

For snRNA-seq datasets, the single cell browser integrates interactive plots of cell type clusters, gene expression, cell type abundance, and marker gene expression. Users can query by gene name, compare gene expression, and filter by cell type or metadata field. Differential gene expression analyses are available for both pseudobulk snRNA-seq and for bulk RNA-seq data.

Finally, gene queries provide gene functions, ontologies, and pathways; links to external resources; and aggregated summaries of gene expression.

 

Who develops MATKP?

MATKP is developed by a multidisciplinary team of researchers and clinicians from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Evan Rosen and Linus Tsai), the University of Chicago (Margo Emont), and the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard (Melina Claussnitzer, Orr Ashenberg, Noël Burtt, and Jason Flannick). MATKP is funded by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (RC2 DK116691).

 

What will MATKP offer in the future?

MATKP is an actively developing resource, so stay tuned for future updates. We plan to expand MATKP with additional datasets, species (e.g., nonhuman primates), and features, including:

  • Epigenomics data
    • ATAC-seq
    • ChIP-seq
    • CUT&RUN
  • Transcriptomics data
    • Single cell RNA-seq
    • Bulk RNA-seq
  • Spatial RNA-seq
  • TRAP-seq
  • Proteomics
  • Metabolomics
  • Imaging (e.g., LipocyteProfiler)

How can I get involved?

MATKP is a growing resource that strives to create an inclusive community for adipose biology. As we develop MATKP, we welcome collaborations in areas including data collection and curation, method development, tool creation, and data visualization. We value input from data providers, experts, and multidisciplinary users to ensure the utility and relevance of our resource. To collaborate, please contact us at help@kp4cd.org. Contribute to the growing body of adipose-related knowledge by submitting your data to the MATKP here.
